comment: Intended sync/async twin divergences. `parity`: pair -> normalised function name -> {reason, sha256 of the normalised diff} (tests/test_twin_parity.py). `raises`: class couple -> normalised method -> {reason, sync, async} declared Raises: sets (tests/test_twin_raises.py). Every entry needs a reason; stale and dead entries fail the guards.

ApicSession.__init__.reason: Async-only bounded fan-out: max_concurrent parameter, its validation and the asyncio.Semaphore; the token lock is threading.Lock vs asyncio.Lock.

ApicSession.max_concurrent.reason: Async-only property exposing the fan-out bound (no sync counterpart: the sync session is not a concurrency driver).

ApicSession._request_with_retry.reason: Two retry shapes: sync `for attempt in stamina.retry_context(...)` vs async nested `@stamina.retry` closure. To converge on `async for attempt in stamina.retry_context(...)` in L8.3.

ApicSession._get_all_pages.reason: Cosmetic: nested comprehension (sync) vs explicit extend loop (async) over the same page iterator. To converge in L8.3.

ApicSession._request_checked.reason: Semaphore only: the async GET runs under `self._semaphore` (max_concurrent is async-only). The reactive re-login (stale token captured before the request, then _reactive_relogin(stale)) must be identical on both sides — this fingerprint is the post-fix shape.

ApicSession._raw_write.reason: Semaphore only: the async write runs under `self._semaphore` (max_concurrent is async-only). The reactive re-login (stale token captured before the request, then _reactive_relogin(stale)) must be identical on both sides — this fingerprint is the post-fix shape.

RawSubscription.__init__.reason: Concurrency by design: queue.Queue vs asyncio.Queue, and the GC finaliser (the async one also captures the running loop to hop back onto it).

SubscriptionSocket.__init__.reason: Concurrency by design: threading.Lock + reader/refresh threads + the `_doomed` list (sync) vs asyncio.Lock + reader/refresh tasks (async); per-flavour socket finaliser.

SubscriptionSocket._connect.reason: Async-only: the connection is opened outside the state lock (a cooperative asyncio.Lock held across a slow connect would stall every coroutine waiting on the socket); the sync twin opens under the lock in _open_socket_locked.

SubscriptionSocket._open_socket_locked.reason: Sync-only: opens the blocking WebSocket under the state lock; the async twin connects outside the lock via _connect.

SubscriptionSocket._ensure_open.reason: Connection outside the lock in async (connect, then re-check _closed/_ws under the lock and discard a losing socket) vs under the lock in sync; threads vs tasks for the reader and refresh loops.

SubscriptionSocket._drop_registration_no.reason: Async-only: the loop-side drop scheduled by the async GC finaliser (call_soon_threadsafe); the sync twin defers through `_doomed`, drained by its refresh thread.

SubscriptionSocket._dispatch.reason: The async socket reads its registry without the state lock: this is a plain `def` with no await point, so it is atomic on the event loop, and an asyncio.Lock cannot be taken from synchronous code. The sync twin must lock (reader/refresh threads mutate the registry concurrently).

SubscriptionSocket._subscription_info_fo.reason: The async socket reads its registry without the state lock: this is a plain `def` with no await point, so it is atomic on the event loop, and an asyncio.Lock cannot be taken from synchronous code. The sync twin must lock (reader/refresh threads mutate the registry concurrently).

SubscriptionSocket._wire_id_for.reason: The async socket reads its registry without the state lock: this is a plain `def` with no await point, so it is atomic on the event loop, and an asyncio.Lock cannot be taken from synchronous code. The sync twin must lock (reader/refresh threads mutate the registry concurrently).

SubscriptionSocket.list_subscriptions.reason: The async socket reads its registry without the state lock: this is a plain `def` with no await point, so it is atomic on the event loop, and an asyncio.Lock cannot be taken from synchronous code. The sync twin must lock (reader/refresh threads mutate the registry concurrently).

SubscriptionSocket.refresh_one_now.reason: The async socket reads its registry without the state lock: this is a plain `def` with no await point, so it is atomic on the event loop, and an asyncio.Lock cannot be taken from synchronous code. The sync twin must lock (reader/refresh threads mutate the registry concurrently).

SubscriptionSocket.subscribe.reason: queue.Queue (sync) vs asyncio.Queue (async) for the new registration's event queue.

SubscriptionSocket._fail_all.reason: The socket handle tracks the blocking WebSocket (`ws`, sync) vs its raw OS socket (`sock`, async, shut down by the finaliser).

SubscriptionSocket._reconnect_and_resubs.reason: Async reconnects outside the state lock through a nested `@stamina.retry` closure and installs the socket afterwards; sync reconnects under the lock with stamina.retry_context; ws vs sock handle.

SubscriptionSocket.close.reason: Async close cancels and awaits its reader/refresh tasks (sync threads are daemons that exit on the generation/closed check); ws vs sock handle.

_refresh_loop.reason: Sync-only drain of `_doomed` (registrations of garbage-collected subscriptions, deferred by the sync finaliser); the async finaliser schedules _drop_registration_nowait on the loop instead.

_finalize_raw_subscription.reason: GC finalisers differ by design: sync appends to `_doomed` (the refresh thread drains it); async hops onto the captured loop with call_soon_threadsafe.

_finalize_socket.reason: GC finalisers differ by design: sync closes the blocking WebSocket; async shuts down the raw OS socket (no loop is available in a finaliser). Message names the right context manager.

_fail_from_crash.reason: Wording only: the crashed background worker is a thread (sync) vs a task (async).

Query.__iter__.reason: Async-only trap: AsyncQuery.__iter__ raises TypeError so `for x in async_query` fails loudly instead of iterating a coroutine; AsyncQuery.__aiter__ carries the real iteration.

Niwaki.__init__.reason: Async-only max_concurrent parameter, validated by the shared session-options helper and kept for the max_concurrent property.

Niwaki.connect.reason: Async-only max_concurrent parameter, forwarded to the constructor.

Niwaki.gather.reason: Async-only fan-out helper (asyncio.TaskGroup); the sync façade has no coroutine to gather.

Niwaki.max_concurrent.reason: Async-only property exposing the fan-out bound.

Niwaki._sync_session.reason: Error message names the right entry point for each flavour (Niwaki.connect()/`with` vs `async with`).

push.reason: Async-only concurrency: the push bound (max_concurrent capped by the client's) feeds verify's concurrency and the bounded wave pool; the sync push runs waves serially through an inline executor.

_refine_part.reason: The sync twin factors the bare GET into _fetch_bare_sync; the async twin inlines the same probe (NotFoundError -> no current object).

_fetch_bare.reason: Sync-only helper of _refine_part_sync (the async twin inlines it).

verify.reason: Async-only bounded concurrency (asyncio.Semaphore + TaskGroup); the sync twin fetches the same sorted unique DNs serially.

_run_waves.reason: Intended: the async wave runner is a bounded worker pool over an AsyncMoWriter (max_concurrent, slots, gather); the sync runner executes each wave serially through a callable. Skip-on-failed-ancestor logic is shared in shape.

__iter__.reason: Async-only trap: AsyncQuery.__iter__ raises TypeError so synchronous iteration of an async query fails loudly; the sync Query iterates for real and raises nothing of its own.
